subject: Admin: How to unsubscribe and make other changes to list settings

messages.subject: Admin: How to unsubscribe and make other changes to list settings
parts:
Dear distance-sampling list members,

There has been a spate of people trying to unsubscribe from the list by
posting messages to distance...@jiscmail.ac.uk. As almost all of you
know, this does not work - instead the message is forwarded to 600 or so
list members.

To leave the list, send an email to:
jisc...@jiscmail.ac.uk
with the message:
leave distance-sampling

Do *not* post messages to
distance...@jiscmail.ac.uk
unless you mean them to be sent to all list members.

Alternatively, you can leave the list by browsing to
http://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/
and clicking on the "Subscriber's Corner" link. Note that you can also
change your list membership settings in the Subscriber's Corner -- e.g., you
can temporarily disable your membership while you're away, or choose to
receive messages in a compact "digest" format.

I am appending the list guidelines, which are sent to all members when they
join. They contain useful information, such as how to leave the list and
guidelines for appropriate messages, so please save them somewhere safe and
read them before posting to the list.

Thanks!

- Len Thomas


************************************
* DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK *
************************************

PLEASE SAVE THIS MESSAGE FOR FUTURE REFERENCE,
IT CONTAINS VITAL INFORMATION

Welcome to the DISTANCE SAMPLING e-mail discussion list. The purpose of
this list is to promote the sharing of ideas and information among
researchers and practitioners interested in distance sampling techniques
(see below). Suitable topics for postings include:

o Questions about distance sampling survey design and analysis.
o New methodological developments in distance sampling.
o Use of software tools (program DISTANCE and other software).
o News about up-coming meetings, workshops and conferences where
distance methods will be discussed.
o Jobs in distance sampling fields.

Instructions for subscribing, unsubscribing, posting and getting help
are given in subsequent sections.

Before posting any messages,

** PLEASE READ THE LIST GUIDELINES **

which are given near the end of this file. Very briefly the key points
are:

o Make sure distance-sampling is the appropriate forum for your message.
If you are unsure ask the list owner first.
o Use informative subject lines.
o If seeking a reply, include your address in the body of your message.
Offer to compile the replies you recieve and summarize them to
the list.
o If replying, consider whether to reply to the sender rather than
the list.
o Send plain text only (no Word or encoded files or other attachments).
o Do not post commercial advertising (however announcements about
jobs, conferences, non-commercial software, etc are okay).


========================================================================
Background
========================================================================

Distance sampling is a widely used technique for estimating the abundance
of biological populations. Distance sampling methods include line
transects, point transects (variable circular plots), cue counting,
trapping webs and migration counts. An introduction to the the
methods is given in the following book:

Buckland, S.T., Anderson, D.R., Burnham, K.P., Laake, J.L., Borchers, D.L,
and Thomas, L. (2001). Introduction to Distance Sampling. Oxford University
Press, Oxford, UK.

A previous edition of the book is freely available for download on the
internet
at http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/

Recent methodological developments and applications are also discussed in
biological journals such as the Journal of Wildlife Management, Ecology,
Biometrics, and the Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Ecological
Statistics.

The standard software for the design and analysis of distance sampling
data is program Distance. Newer versions are fully windows-based with an
intuitive point-and-click interface. The software is freely available for
download from the Distance home page http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/


========================================================================
Important Email Addresses
========================================================================

1. distance...@jiscmail.ac.uk

This is the address of this list. Any messages sent to this address
will be automatically forwarded to all the members of the list.

2. jisc...@jiscmail.ac.uk

This is the JISCmail program. You send commands (such as
join distance-sampling) to this address.

3. distance-sam...@jiscmail.ac.uk

This is the address for the list owner who looks after the list
(currently Len Thomas of the University of St Andrews, UK).

If you have a problem with the list, send a message to this address.

For example,
- if you have problems leaving the list
- if you have problems sending a message to the list

4. jiscmail...@jiscmail.ac.uk

This is the JISCmail Helpline.
If you have any questions about or problems with the JISCmail system
use this address.


========================================================================
Important World-Wide Web sites
========================================================================

1. http://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/lists/distance-sampling.html

This is the list home page. Here you will find information about
the list (this file), an archive of all messages to the list over the
past year, and other files that I may post from time to time.

2. http://www.jiscmail.ac.uk

JISCmail home page. From here you can find out more about how to
manage your list membership, and about the other lists run by the
JISCmail server.


========================================================================
How to...
========================================================================

1. To send a message to everyone on the list, send an email to:
distance...@jiscmail.ac.uk

2. To leave distance-sampling, send an email to:
jisc...@jiscmail.ac.uk
with the message:
leave distance-sampling
--

3. To join distance-sampling, send an email to:
jisc...@jiscmail.ac.uk
with the message:
join distance-sampling yourfirstname yourlastname
--
Replace the text "yourfirstname" with your first name and the text
"yourlastname" with your last name
(e.g., join distance-sampling Joan Smith)

4. To find out more about what the JISCmail server can do (for example
searching the monthly archive of messages, suspending mail when you're
on holiday, etc):
a) Check out the web pages at http://www.jiscmail.ac.uk especially
http://jiscmail.ac.uk/docs/user-ref-card.html
b) Send an e-mail to:
jisc...@jiscmail.ac.uk
with the message:
info
--
You will then received a list of on-line documentation about
JISCmail, and you can use the "get" command to retrieve those
documents which interest you. For example, the message:
get JISCUSER.REFCARD
will get you the user reference card.


========================================================================
List Guidelines
========================================================================

Please bear in mind that posting a message to distance-sampling is
equivalent to sending several hundred people individual e-mail messages.
The list is intended to facilitate the sharing of ideas and information,
but if there are too many messages then people will become overwhelmed
and leave the list, so defeating its purpose.

To make each posting as informative as possible, please observe the
following guidelines:

1. Make sure distance-sampling is the appropriate forum for your post.
If your message is not specifically about distance sampling methods,
it belongs somewhere else. An excellent list of statistical lists is
maintained by Stuart Young at http://www.stats.gla.ac.uk/allstat/
A comprehensive, if somewhat out-of-date list of ecological lists was
written by Una Smith and is archived in many places including
http://immwww.jr2.ox.ac.uk/bioguide/ If you are unsure whether your
message is appropriate, send it to the list owner (distance-sampling-
req...@jiscmail.ac.uk) and ask him to tell you.

2. Use informative subject lines.
This will enable people to decide whether your message is of interest
to them, so they can choose whether to read it or not. Everyone is
busy, and messages with uninformative subject lines like "Question",
"Test", "Distance sampling", etc., will probably get deleted by many
people without even being read. Try and make your subject lines
concice but informative, e.g., "g(0) for double-platform minke whale
transects", "Design of VCPs for forest bird surveys", "Workshop: Intro
to distance sampling, New Zealand".

3. If you are asking a question, make sure you have done your homework
first.
Sending a message to several hundred people without putting in at least
a days work on the problem yourself first is rude. There is a lot of
information available about distance sampling which should be consulted
before posting a message, for example the book Introduction to Distance
Sampling by Buckland et al. (http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance).
If you have joined the list recently, you should also check the archives
to see that the question has not been discussed already (archives are at
http://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/lists/distance-sampling.html).

4. If you are asking a question, consider requesting that replies are sent
to your e-mail address, and offer to summarize the ensuing discussion
to the list.
By encouraging list members who are interested in your question to mail
you directly, a discussion can be initiated that is not constrained
by the need to keep the volume of list e-mail down. If you then post
a summary of this discussion to the list then eveyone will be able to
read the comments in a concise format, and you may well get further
advice from people. This is especially appropriate if you have a
question that you think will be of minority interest.

5. If you want any replies, include your name and e-mail address your
message.
Some e-mail programs don't let people find this information out unless
it is in the body of your message. Having a "signature" that is
appended to the bottom of all messages is a good idea, so long as it is
short.

6. If you are replying, consider whether to reply to the sender rather
than the list.
If you are sure your answer is correct, and it will be of general
interest then by all means post to the list. Otherwise, consider
sending it directly to the person who asked the question and asking
them to summarize the replies they receive to the list.
Double check where your reply is going to. Look in both the To: field
and the cc: fields - if either says distance...@jiscmail.ac.uk
then your reply will go to the list.

7. Send plain text only (no Word or encoded files or other attachments).
Why no attachments? (i) Many of the people on the list will not be
interested in your particular question, so will not want to see the
dataset/screengrab you are posting. This is frustrating for them if
they spent many minutes downloading your message down a telephone line.
(ii) Many members have a limit on the size of their inbox, so sending a
large attachment can crash their mail system, or prevent them from
receiving any other messages. (iii) Many mail reading programs cannot
deal with attachments, and your message shows up on such systems as a
seemingly random series of ASCII text.
If you want to post extra information, such as data files or screen
shots, what should you do? (i) If you have access to a web server, the
easiest thing is to upload the file there and provide the URL (web
address) in your *plain text* message, so that people can download it
if they want. (ii) You can do a similar thing if you have an anonymous
ftp server - include instructions for accessing the file in your message.
(iii) If you have none of there, offer to email the file to anyone who
asks you for it. You will be surprised how few people do! However,
this way, you can be sure that it will reach those who are interested.

8. Do not post commercial advertising.
The list is not a forum for posting unsolicted adverts to people.
Announcements about job vacancies, conferences, workshops and non-
commercial software releases are fine. If there is any doubt, send
the message to the list owner and it will be forwarded to the list if
it is appropriate.


========================================================================
Troubleshooting
========================================================================

o Never send commands, or requests to join, or admin. queries, to
distance...@jiscmail.ac.uk - your problem will be broadcast to
all members of the list!

o If something goes wrong - perhaps you get two copies of every message -
send a message to distance-sam...@jiscmail.ac.uk

o If your mail address changes, send a message to
distance-sam...@jiscmail.ac.uk

o If mail from distance-sampling to you is regularly rejected for some
reason (perhaps because you have run out of file space or your computer
mail service has been renamed) the list-owner may eventually delete you
from the list.

o If you get no mail, you may have been deleted from the list - see above.
Either send a message to distance-sam...@jiscmail.ac.uk, or
resubscribe
